subject: Clarifying private-offer invoicing & commercial paths for AWS/Azure/GCP listings
messages:
From: Lisa Zhang <lzhang@novacorp.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplaceops@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions - NovaCorp marketplace procurement pathing

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team at Nova loved the latency and the billing flexibility you showed. Procurement asked me to get a few practical clarifications so they can pick the right purchasing path (AWS Private Offer vs Azure SaaS Metered vs GCP Marketplace SaaS). Can you confirm the following for Redwood?

1) Invoicing flow: if we go with an AWS Private Offer, will NovaCorp receive an invoice directly from Redwood or from AWS? What about consolidated billing for multiple accounts?

2) PO acceptance: can Redwood accept a standard NovaCorp PO (we have a referenced PO template) and will Redwood sign a PO that references a private offer?

3) Tax & remittance: who is the tax-collecting party for each marketplace path?

4) Metering/crediting: for SaaS metered products, is Redwood able to report usage to the marketplace marketplace meter on a daily cadence? Is there a reconciliation process you support?

5) Evidence for procurement: procurement wants a short matrix for who provides the invoice, where data residency is logged, and where the contract resides (Redwood vs marketplace). If you can attach a one-pager or spreadsheet that maps this across AWS/Azure/GCP, that would be ideal.

We are aiming for a purchasing window in the first week of April. Can you get back with the answers and any attachments we can share with Nova procurement?

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Zhang
Senior Procurement Manager, NovaCorp

If there's one immediate note: Redwood can accept a NovaCorp PO and will sign POs that reference private offers, but there are some standard addenda for marketplace terms we usually include — we'll flag that in the doc.

Best,

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial questions - NovaCorp marketplace procurement pathing

Team — draft answers below (I populated the matrix and attached as "marketplace_procurement_answers_v1.xlsx"). Please review and add details where needed.

AWS Private Offer:
- Invoice party: Redwood invoices NovaCorp directly (we also can route invoices through AWS if Nova requires consolidated AWS billing — that is set up as an account-level arrangement; invoicing via AWS means the payment first goes to AWS who remits to Redwood per marketplace settlement timelines).
- PO acceptance: Yes, Redwood accepts customer POs referencing a private offer; we require the PO to reference the private offer ID and standard PO addendum for marketplace revenue share.
- Tax: Redwood collects tax where we are the merchant of record unless Nova elects to buy via AWS (then AWS handles tax remittance in certain regions). We will provide tax certificates as part of onboarding.
- Metering: Redwood can push usage events daily to AWS Marketplace metering service. Reconciliation is supported via our billing ops and we provide a monthly usage export and a reconciliation spreadsheet.

Azure SaaS Metered:
- Invoice party: Typically Redwood invoices Nova directly. If Nova wants Microsoft to handle invoicing, we can do an offer that routes billing through MS commerce; that requires 60–90 days to set up and a reseller agreement.
- PO acceptance: We accept PO; Azure requires additional commerce terms and Microsoft may require signed reseller paperwork.
- Tax: Commerce partner rules apply; often Microsoft is merchant of record depending on the commerce path.
- Metering: We support metering via Azure Marketplace APIs; cadence can be daily or weekly depending on product packaging.

GCP SaaS (Marketplace):
- Invoice party: Redwood invoices customer directly for most SaaS SaaS listings. GCP Billing (if used) can consolidate invoices; GCP remits to us according to their payout schedule.
- PO acceptance: Yes; GCP sometimes mandates additional commercial terms for entitlements if using Google-managed billing.
- Tax: Similar split — Redwood collects tax unless GCP is the commerce party in a managed billing arrangement.
- Metering: We can send usage and reconciliation files to GCP marketplace; daily reporting supported for metered SKUs.

Attached I included: marketplace_procurement_answers_v1.xlsx (matrix + notes), a draft PO template (draft_po_template.docx), and a screenshot of the proposed pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_screenshot.png).

Priya — can you validate the PO addendum language and confirm the DocuSign flow? Marissa, can you confirm typical settlement lead times for AWS private offers (we usually see 30–60 days). Ben — anything to add on tax or VAT handling for EU customers (Nova currently will be US-only for this purchase, but good to be explicit).

Thanks,
Karthik

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial questions - NovaCorp marketplace procurement pathing

Quick confirmations:
- AWS private offer settlement: typical payout to Redwood is 30–45 days after AWS processes the purchase. We sometimes see 60 days on large enterprise arrangements if AWS needs extended credit terms.
- DocuSign flow: We will send a standard Redwood Order Form + PO addendum via DocuSign. The DocuSign link in the related_links folder is our standard powerform for marketplace offers.
- Consolidated billing: If Nova wants consolidated AWS billing across multiple internal accounts, they must provide payer account ID and we map SKUs to that account. That does not block acceptance of a PO; it is a billing config step.

I'll add a short paragraph to the matrix about expected timing for setup (30–90 days depending on commerce path).

Marissa
Director, Marketplace Go-to-Market

Priya — this is very helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from procurement after reviewing the matrix:

- Can Redwood confirm the template language we should expect on the PO addendum (specifically around revenue share and liability carve-outs)? We want to pre-clear legal to avoid last-minute redlines.
- For AWS private offers: if we choose consolidated billing via AWS, will our invoices still show Redwood line items or will they be rolled up? Procurement prefers line-level visibility on the AWS invoice if possible.

We attached Nova's PO template to this thread separately; procurement asked us to test filling it with Redwood details — would you prefer we upload it to your Drive folder or send it directly?

If you can respond by EOD Thursday Pacific, procurement can start internal approvals next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround — Nova is looking to close the purchase before their fiscal quarter close.

Best,
Lisa
